metric_definitions.name: Mean squared error
metric_definitions.definition: Mean of squared differences between reconstructed and input pixels, with images resized to 200x200 and scaled to [0, 1] (Sections 2.2, 4, 5.1). Averaged over the 2,900-image validation set.
metric_definitions.unresolved: The paper does not say whether the mean is over all pixels and channels (torch MSELoss default) or a mean of per-batch losses, nor whether the feedforward model is scored on grayscale (Figure 1 shows a 40,000-value input, i.e. 200x200x1) or RGB images.
metric_definitions.implementation: mean of squared differences between reconstruction and input over all pixels (and channels) of the validation images, pixel values in [0, 1]
metric_definitions.version: not reported by the paper; this attempt will use torch.nn.functional.mse_loss (reduction='mean') summed per batch and divided by the total element count
metric_definitions.aggregation: single value over the 2,900-image validation set; one training run per model, no seeds or repeats reported
metric_definitions.unit_or_scale: squared pixel intensity on the [0, 1] scale

experiments.description: Train each of the three autoencoders on 11,600 training images (80% of 500 per class) with Adam and MSE loss; report validation MSE on the remaining 2,900 images.

paper_protocol.data: 500 images per class x 29 classes, 80/20 split into 11,600 train / 2,900 validation (Section 4; Section 5.1 gives 2,900 validation images selected with a fixed random seed). Section 2.1's 69,600/17,400 split of all 87,000 images conflicts with this; the 2,900 figure is used because Section 5.1 ties it to the evaluation.
paper_protocol.optimizer: Adam; loss MSE. Learning rate, batch size, epochs, seed and checkpoint selection are not reported.
paper_protocol.feedforward: Fully connected; Figure 1 shows flattened input of 40,000 values, two hidden layers each side and a 64-d latent. Hidden widths, activations and the output activation are not reported.
paper_protocol.convolutional: Three 4x4 stride-2 padding-1 convolutions 3->32->64->128 (200->100->50->25), flatten 25x25x128, linear to 64; mirrored decoder with linear and transposed convolutions; ReLU throughout, sigmoid output. The paper states about 16 million parameters; this specification gives 10,651,139.
paper_protocol.diffusion: Convolutional encoder producing mean and variance through fully connected layers; 100-timestep beta noise schedule on the latent; a fully connected denoiser 'with five primary layers, multiple dynamically added layers, and final output layers'; convolutional decoder from the denoised latent; about 16 million parameters. Latent size, beta schedule, denoiser widths, the 'dynamically added layers', the loss composition (reconstruction, noise prediction, KL) and how reconstructions are produced at evaluation are not reported. Figure 3 is the latent diffusion (Stable Diffusion) overview diagram, not this model.

experiments.checkpoint_rule: not reported; Section 4 says the model is saved 'after training', read as the final-epoch weights

gates.reason: No code exists, and the paper omits details that change the reported MSE: training hyperparameters and seeds for all three models, which 500 images per class are used, the entire feedforward architecture apart from its 40,000-value input and 64-d latent, and almost all of the diffusion model.
evidence: Section 4 states only 'Adam optimizer', 'MSE loss', 'multiple epochs', '500 images per class' and an 80/20 split.
Sections 3.1 and 3.2 repeat the same paragraph and give no feedforward layer sizes; Figure 1 shows the input size (40,000) and latent size (64) only.
Section 3.6 describes the diffusion denoiser as 'five primary layers, multiple dynamically added layers, and final output layers' without sizes, schedule values or loss terms.
Section 3.4's specification gives 10,651,139 parameters, not the stated ~16 million, so the convolutional model as described is not exactly the model that was run.
gates.required_action: Human decision: either authorise a labelled conditional reimplementation with documented guesses (results kept as conditional evidence, targets not marked produced), or close the attempt as insufficient_information without training.
gates.resolution: The assigning user authorised a labelled conditional reimplementation of all three models with documented guesses. The missing protocol details remain unknown, so the runs are conditional evidence and the targets are not produced.

guesses.detail: Which 500 images per class, and how the 80/20 split is drawn
guesses.paper: '500 images per class ... 80/20 split' (Section 4); validation of 2,900 images 'randomly selected ... using a fixed random seed' (Section 5.1); seed not given
guesses.used: random.Random(42).sample of 500 sorted filenames per class, then a torch.randperm(seed 42) 80/20 split of the pooled 14,500 images (11,600 / 2,900; split.json sha256 80d17c24...)
guesses.effect: Behaviour-changing: a different subset changes the validation MSE.

guesses.detail: Learning rate, batch size, epochs, seed, checkpoint
guesses.paper: Adam, MSE loss, 'multiple epochs'; weights saved after training
guesses.used: Adam lr 1e-3, batch 32, 20 epochs, seed 42, final-epoch weights, fp32

guesses.paper: Figure 1: flattened 40,000-value input and output, two hidden layers per side, 64-d latent; nothing else
guesses.used: Grayscale 200x200 input (40,000 values, following Figure 1); 40000-1024-256-64-256-1024-40000 with ReLU and a sigmoid output (82,519,680 parameters)
guesses.effect: Behaviour-changing; the feedforward MSE is computed on grayscale pixels while the other two models use RGB.

guesses.detail: Activation after the decoder's linear layer
guesses.paper: ReLU on every convolution and transposed convolution, sigmoid on the output; linear layers not specified
guesses.used: ReLU after the decoder linear layer, none after the encoder linear layer (10,651,139 parameters vs the paper's 'approximately 16 million')
guesses.effect: Minor; the parameter-count mismatch shows the paper's model differs from its own description in some unknown way.

guesses.paper: Section 3.6: mean/variance heads, 100-step beta schedule on the latent, FC denoiser with 'five primary layers, multiple dynamically added layers, and final output layers'; ~16 million parameters
guesses.used: 64-d latent with reparameterised sampling; linear betas 1e-4 to 0.02 over 100 steps; one random timestep per image; five 256-wide ReLU layers plus an output layer predicting the noise from (z_t, t/100); z0 estimated from the predicted noise and decoded; loss = reconstruction MSE + noise MSE, no KL; evaluation uses the same stochastic forward pass with a fixed generator seed (16,067,715 parameters)
guesses.effect: Behaviour-changing and the largest source of uncertainty. Only the parameter count is checkable, and it matches the paper.

guesses.used: Sum of squared errors over every pixel and channel divided by the element count
guesses.effect: Equal to the mean of per-image MSE here because all images have the same size.

deviations.detail: Section 2.1 describes an 80/20 split of all 87,000 images (69,600/17,400); Sections 4 and 5.1 describe 500 images per class and a 2,900-image validation set.
deviations.used: The 500-per-class protocol, because Section 5.1 ties the 2,900-image validation set to the reported MSE.
deviations.effect: Recorded as the paper's own inconsistency, not a choice of this attempt.
